description: Composite ex-situ XRD figure (six panels) on 35 h mechanically milled Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high-entropy steel powder. (a) Stacked full patterns at R.T., 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C, plotted as Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (Degree) from 20 to 100°, with phase markers ▼ BCC, ▲ B2-type, ♣ γ-brass type and ● Fe5Si3-type. The strongest reflection lies between the 40 and 50° ticks (seen enlarged in b), with further peaks near 65° and 82°; the R.T. pattern is the broadest. (b) Vertically offset enlargement of the 42°-46° range for the same five temperatures, resolving a BCC (▼) maximum, a B2 (◇) shoulder and γ-brass (♣) plus Fe5Si3 (●) markers. (c-e) Deconvoluted fits of the 400 °C, 500 °C and 600 °C patterns over 2θ ≈ 43-47° (500 °C over 44-46°), each decomposing the black measured profile into teal B2, red BCC and blue γ-brass components. (f) Enlarged 800 °C pattern from 40° to 46° with a green Fe5Si3-type peak near 41.7°, a γ-brass feature near 43° and two resolved maxima labelled B2 (◇) and BCC (▼). Together the panels show the milled powder is stable to 500 °C, Fe5Si3-type (hP16) intermetallic forms at 600 °C and grows to 800 °C, with increased B2 fraction at 800 °C.

subfigures.description: Stacked full-range ex-situ XRD patterns for R.T., 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C, Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (Degree) from 20 to 100°, with a legend assigning ▼ BCC, ▲ B2-type, ♣ γ-brass type and ● Fe5Si3-type; the dominant reflection sits between the 40 and 50° ticks and the R.T. trace is the broadest.

Vertically offset enlargement of the same five traces over 2θ = 42-46°, resolving the BCC (▼) peak, the B2 (◇) shoulder at lower angle and γ-brass (♣) / Fe5Si3 (●) markers; peaks sharpen from R.T. to 800 °C.

Deconvolution of the 400 °C pattern over 2θ = 43-47°: the black measured profile is fitted by a teal B2-type component, a red BCC component and a small blue γ-brass component; legend ♣ γ-brass type, ▼ BCC, ◇ B2 type.

Deconvolution of the 500 °C pattern over 2θ = 44-46° showing three fitted components (teal B2-type, red BCC, blue γ-brass) under the black measured curve; the γ-brass component is clearly resolved on the high-angle side.
Deconvolution of the 600 °C pattern over 2θ = 43-47°, again fitted as teal B2-type plus red BCC dominates with a small blue γ-brass component.

Enlarged 800 °C pattern from 2θ = 40-46° with legend ▼ BCC, ◇ B2 type, ♣ γ-brass type, ● Fe5Si3 type: a green Fe5Si3-type peak near 41.7°, a γ-brass (♣) feature near 43° and two clearly resolved maxima with B2 (◇) and BCC (▼) markers.

observations.observation: Panel (a) stacks five full XRD traces labelled R.T., 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C, with Intensity (a.u.) on the ordinate and 2θ (Degree) from 20 to 100 on the abscissa.
The panel (a) legend assigns ▼ to BCC, ▲ to B2-type, ♣ to γ-brass type and ● to Fe5Si3-type.
Panel (b) is a vertically offset enlargement of the 42°-46° 2θ window for all five temperatures, showing that the main reflection progressively sharpens from R.T. to 800 °C.
Panels (c), (d) and (e) each show a black measured profile fitted by three deconvoluted components coloured teal (B2 type), red (BCC) and dark blue (γ-brass type).
Panel (f), the 800 °C enlargement over 2θ = 40-46°, displays a green Fe5Si3-type peak near 41.7° and two resolved maxima in the 44-45° region marked with B2 (◇) and BCC (▼) symbols.
The caption labels the panels (c-e) as deconvoluted peaks for the 400 °C, 500 °C and 600 °C samples respectively, and panel (f) as an enlarged view of the 800 °C pattern over 40°-46°.
The caption writes the new phase as 'Fe Si-type' while the in-figure legends print 'Fe5Si3-type' (and 'Fe5Si3 type' in panel f) - the two wordings differ.
The citing text states that the exothermic event at ~520 °C corresponds to formation of the Fe Si-type phase (Figs. 4 & 5(e)).
The citing text states that the 35 h milled powder is thermally stable up to 500 °C and that the Fe Si-type intermetallic phase (hP16) evolves at 600 °C and grows further up to 800 °C.
The citing text states that at 800 °C no phase change occurs but the amount of the B2-type phase increases.
The citing text attributes the ~420 °C exothermic event to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase (Figs. 4 & 5(d)).
The caption states that the formation of the Fe Si-type intermetallic phase at 600 °C correlates with the exothermic event at 520 °C in Fig. 4.
No diffraction angle or intensity value is printed as a number on any data point; only axis ticks (2θ 20-100°, 42-46°, 43-47°, 40-46°) are available as quantitative anchors.
